prs.title: Trap volatiles in the solid mantle behind the freezing front
prs.author: IKisvardai
prs.body: ## Description Adds solid-phase volatile trapping during mantle crystallisation. The trapped melt fraction comes from the drainage of pore melt across the freezing front that the Aragog interior resolves. Relates to #519. `outgas.trap_mode` takes `'none'` (default) or `'front'`. With `'none'` the trapping step does not run, desiccation and the escape floor act as on main, and the per-element closure check is not applied. One fix applies with trapping off as well: a frozen mantle's atmosphere is now debited by what escape took from each element total (see Bookkeeping), where main left 1.8e-5 of every step's loss in the atmosphere with CALLIOPE. The golden trajectory differs from main only by new constant-zero columns, and a helpfile written by main resumes on this branch. ### Physics - **Mass balance.** Each crystallisation step moves `[(1 - F_tl) D_Z + F_tl] C_Z dM_RM` of every dissolved species from the melt into the solid mantle (Sim, Hirschmann & Hier-Majumder 2024, Eq. 6). Here: - `C_Z` is the concentration from the previous chemistry solve, taken on the melt it dissolved into; - `dM_RM = M_mantle [Phi(t-1) - Phi(t)]`; - `D_Z` comes from `outgas.D_const_ `. Water is 0.0017 and every other species is 0, so the others are buried through the interstitial melt alone. That includes the noble gases dissolved in the melt, at `F_tl C_Z dM_RM`. The step is capped at what the melt holds. - **Trapped melt fraction.** The front runs from the node where the solver's melt fraction cros

prs.title: Move the agent instructions to AGENTS.md
prs.author: egpbos
prs.body: ## Description This builds on Patrick's trim of the agent instructions and moves them to the `AGENTS.md` format, which most coding agents read. The root `AGENTS.md` holds the rules for the repository and `tests/AGENTS.md` the rules for tests; `CLAUDE.md` and `tests/CLAUDE.md` import them, and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` keeps a short checklist that points to `AGENTS.md`. Longer review notes are in `.github/agent-rules/code-review.md`, and `.github/.claude/rules/` is gone. The rules that every PROTEUS module shares (units at module boundaries, physics tests that fail for the most plausible wrong formula, commit and pull-request text, inline comments of at most 4 lines) have one canonical copy in `tools/agents/core.md` and `tools/agents/tests-core.md`. `tools/agents/sync_core.py` writes them into a repository's `AGENTS.md` files with their sha256, and `tools/agents/check_agents_md.py` fails when a shared block no longer matches its hash or is missing, when a file exceeds its size limit (16,000 B at the root, 12,000 B in `tests/`), or when a `CLAUDE.md` does not import its `AGENTS.md`. The check runs in pre-commit and in the PR checks and replaces `tools/check_file_sizes.sh`. A daily workflow (`.github/workflows/agents-md-sync.yml`) clones the module repositories and runs both tools on each one that carries an `AGENTS.md`, so a module that lags behind or carries a damaged block turns it red; it is separate from the nightly, so a pending sync does not affect the PR coverage

prs.title: Fetch reference data through fwl-io and require the tables each run reads
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description PROTEUS now fetches and reads its reference data through fwl-io manifests, in the versioned FWL_DATA layout: SOCRATES spectral files, solar, Named, MUSCLES and PHOENIX stellar spectra, the Hammond surface spectra, the Seager and Zalmoxis EOS tables, the melting curves and the P-S lookup tables. It also sets which tables a Zalmoxis run needs and stops a run with missing data before it starts. Closes #905, closes #907. Changes: - Every dataset is fetched through fwl-io and verified against its pinned checksums; multi-model datasets come from the fwl-io shared manifest. Requires fwl-io and fwl-mors 26.9.23. - A run requires exactly the PALEOS tables its EOS reads: the layer tables of every component, the MgSiO3 2-phase pair when the energetics or a `liquidus_super` anchor read it, and PALEOS-API tables resolved at start (the check stops at once when `paleos` is not installed). - One melting curve and one table set per run. With SPIDER or Aragog, the mantle energetics must follow a PALEOS, WolfBower2018 or RTPress100TPa EOS; a Seager2007, Chabrier or analytic energetics key, two MgSiO3 sources in one mixture, and fractions that are not positive are rejected when the configuration loads. A PALEOS H2O or iron mantle takes the MgSiO3 2-phase energetics, with a warning. - The dummy structure no longer touches the PALEOS tables, and places the P-S tables and melting curves whenever SPIDER or Aragog read them (#905). - Offline, every missing-data stop names its download

prs.title: Grow the planet by giant impacts: the accretion module and Morrigan
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description This adds `accretion`, a module that grows the planet by giant impacts while the magma ocean evolves, and couples Morrigan into PROTEUS as its dynamical implementation. Closes #168. Related to #407, which asks for a parametrised impact mass-loss scaling; the loss used here is the Kegerreis et al. (2020) law evaluated by ZEPHYRUS, not the scaling that issue proposes. An impact is applied at the end of the timestep that lands on its time, so the orbit and structure of that step already use the grown planet. Each collision adds the impactor's rock and re-solves the interior structure at the new mass, delivers the impactor's volatiles while the same collision fraction strips both bodies' atmospheres, re-melts the mantle by re-applying the run's temperature-mode initial condition, and moves the orbit by the impact's change in semi-major axis and eccentricity, clamped to a bound orbit. The whole-planet mass closes to before plus rock plus delivered minus stripped, which can be a net shrink when a small impactor blows off a heavier atmosphere. Three implementations: - `morrigan` follows a system of embryos through the giant-impact phase with the semi-analytical Monte Carlo model of Kimura et al. (2025) and hands PROTEUS the impact history of one survivor. - `timeline` replays an impact history from a file, for reproducing a published history or driving PROTEUS from one computed elsewhere. - `dummy` builds a history from scaling laws: exponential approach to an asympto

prs.title: Solve liquidus_super on the interior P-S tables for every structure
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description Closes #883. With `temperature_mode = "liquidus_super"`, a run without a Zalmoxis structure still solved its initial adiabat on the PALEOS P-T curves. In the SPIDER-only config from the issue, that PALEOS entropy (about 10590 J/kg/K) lies far above the Wolf & Bower table maximum (3236 J/kg/K), so SPIDER started at the table edge: T_magma stayed at 3820 K, 1840 to 2700 K above the table liquidus instead of the requested 500 K, and each initial condition ran several PALEOS solves. The initial entropy is now solved on the interior P-S tables against their own liquidus (`liquidus_P-S.dat`), the curve the interior solver uses for its melt fraction, for every structure module: - `spider`, or `dummy` without a PALEOS mantle: the tables come from FWL_DATA or the SPIDER lookup data. No Zalmoxis import and no PALEOS read. - `zalmoxis`, or `dummy` with a PALEOS mantle: Zalmoxis generates the tables from the mantle EOS. The structure solve still anchors its temperature on a P-T adiabat `delta_T_super` above the P-T liquidus, and the initial entropy is capped at that anchor entropy. When the requested superheat cannot be reached before the table edge, the solve clamps to the largest superheat it can reach and a warning reports it, together with the superheat at the deepest node when `ini_dsdr < 0`. prs.title: Add a prune command for dataset versions no longer referenced
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: Add `fwl-io prune`, which removes dataset versions that no installed manifest references any more. Closes #14. Every pin bump leaves the old version directory behind in FWL_DATA, and nothing cleans them up. Since the same tree often holds user runs and is shared between environments, the command is built to keep anything it cannot prove is an old fwl-io download. - `fwl-io prune` prints a plan by default. `--delete` removes the superseded versions after a confirmation (`--yes` skips it), and `--include-orphans` also removes versions under a subdirectory that no installed manifest knows, since on a shared tree those can belong to another environment. - A directory is only a target when it carries a stamp naming its own record and subdirectory, holds no nested version, mount or unreadable part, and no referenced version or symlink inside one points into it. Everything else is reported and kept. - Nothing is deleted when a manifest fails to load, part of the tree cannot be read, or a fetch lock is held. Locks are probed read-only before every removal; lock entries that cannot be probed block, and lock files this user cannot write give a warning. - Each target is checked again right before it is moved into staging and deleted there, and it is put back if it changed. The docs state what prune assumes: no other program reorganises the tree while it runs. - Python API: `plan_prune`, `apply_prune` and `prune_versions`. `resolve_data_root` gets `create=False` so a prune never creates

prs.title: feat(numerics): iteration control, numerical limiters, and slab benchmark
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## What this does This pull request adds iteration controls and numerical limiters to the Stokes-Darcy, thermal, and plastic solvers in Erebus.jl. When plastic yield iterations fail to converge, it rolls back state arrays to a snapshot and halves the timestep. It also bounds temperature increments on every thermal substep, updates the default compaction rate limit, and stops unphysical permeability inversion. In addition, it adds a 2D analytical thermal slab conduction benchmark and a configuration schema verification tool. The changes improve run stability. ## Why Plastic yield iterations can stall near sharp rheological boundaries. This stalls the model. When this occurs, we need to roll back to a clean state and halve the timestep rather than proceed with unconverged stresses. Rapid heating can also violate thermal stability during subcycling, and hydrofracture permeability needs min-max clamping when initial permeability exceeds threshold bounds. The new benchmark verifies physical accuracy against a closed-form solution. The schema tool keeps documentation aligned with code defaults. ## Changes - In `src/physics/poroelasticity.jl`: - Clamp `compute_hydrofracture_permeability` with min-max bounds to prevent inverted scaling when `kphi > kmax`. - Throw a `DomainError` if input matrix permeability is negative. - In `src/numerics/stokes_darcy.jl`: - Exclude the pressure anchor cell at index (2, 2) when finding `aphimax` in `compute_Aϕ!`. - In `src/config.jl`, `src/constants.

prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Summary Add extreme-resolution Stokes-Darcy solver capabilities to enable scaling beyond 2048x2048 grids: - Analytical diagonal Darcy condensation: Reduces the global coupled system from 6 degrees of freedom per node to 4 degrees of freedom by algebraically eliminating Darcy fluxes. Reconstructs Darcy fluxes accurately after the solve, preserving local fluid-mass conservation and hydrofracture permeability modulation via pre-solve effective pressure caching. - MatrixFreeStokesDarcyOperator: Implements 2D staggered-grid matrix-free operator evaluation directly on grid arrays without assembling the global sparse matrix, eliminating sparse matrix memory allocation. - BlockSchurPreconditioner: Implements discrete Poisson Schur complement scaling for pressure degrees of freedom with diagonal velocity scaling for both 4-variable and 6-variable formulations. - LinearSolve Krylov iterative solvers: Adds FGMRES, GMRES, and BiCGStab with convergence validation, configurable tolerances, restart dimensions, and max iterations. - Solver configuration schema: Exposes hydromech_solver, krylov_method, krylov_rtol, krylov_atol, krylov_maxiter, krylov_restart, darcy_elimination, and preconditioner with schema bounds and cross-validation. - Full backward compatibility: darcy_elimination defaults to false and hydromech_solver defaults to :direct, preserving identical floating-point behavior for existing benchmarks. ## Verification - test/test_darcy_elimination.jl: 29 of 29 tests pass, confirm

prs.title: Implement coupled 1D atmosphere, disk envelope capture, and hydrodynamic escape
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Overview During planetesimal differentiation, interior volatile outgassing couples to ambient nebular gas and space environments. Planetesimals embedded in the disk capture ambient nebular gas within their gravitational sphere of influence up to convective recycling limits. During disk dispersal, depressurization drives hydrodynamic boil-off into space. Accumulated volatiles form a greenhouse blanket that attenuates surface radiative cooling and raises surface temperatures according to Guillot (2010) semi-grey radiative equilibrium. When light carrier gases escape hydrodynamically, neutral collisions drag heavier volatile species according to Zahnle and Kasting (1986) crossover mass relations. This pull request implements a coupled 1D proto-atmosphere and envelope solver in Erebus.jl, integrating envelope capture, boil-off during disk dispersal, multi-species optical depth, Guillot semi-grey radiative equilibrium, attenuated surface radiative boundary conditions, and Zahnle-Kasting hydrodynamic crossover escape. ## Key Changes - Atmosphere and Envelope Physics (`src/atmosphere.jl`): - Implement `compute_gravitational_capture_radius` for Bondi and Hill capture limits. - Implement `compute_disk_envelope_mass` with Ormel et al. (2015) 3D recycling cap. - Implement `compute_atmospheric_optical_depth` across multi-species inventories. - Implement `compute_guillot_surface_temperature` for semi-grey irradiated radiative equilibrium. - Implement `compute_effective_radiation_htc` w

prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## What this does Converts oxygen fugacity between canonical mineral and gas equilibria (IW, QFM, NNO, MH, WM, QIF, and CCO). Accounts for electron-equivalent redox budgets in rock and fluid reservoirs following Evans (2012). ## Why Tracks oxidation states during planetesimal growth to model volatile speciation, core metal-silicate equilibria, and outgassing compositions. ## Changes - Add zero-allocation buffer conversions for IW, QFM, NNO, MH, WM, QIF, and CCO in src/redox.jl. - Implement Evans (2012) electron accounting with conservation in core formation, serpentinization, and gas venting. - Add local controlling buffer regime identification. - Add documentation in docs/src/validation/redox_buffers.md. - Add unit and property tests in test/test_redox.jl. - Add format and figure collision validators in tools/. ## Testing - Unit tests: test/test_redox.jl passes (95 assertions). - Full test suite: Pkg.test() passes (397,921 tests). - Reference verification: julia tools/verify_references.jl passes. - Documentation checks: julia tools/check_docs_formatting.jl and python3 tools/check_figure_collisions.py pass.

prs.title: Implement planetesimal accretion engine with expanding marker boundary
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## What this does This implements a planetesimal accretion engine with expanding marker-in-cell boundaries, impact kinetic heating, and protoplanetary disk snowline coupling. It supports Bondi and Hill pebble accretion regimes, Safronov gravitational focusing in planetesimal collision swarms, and analytical mass and radius growth modes. ## Why Accretion delivers mass, energy, and volatile inventories to growing planetesimals during protoplanetary disk evolution. Modeling expanding boundaries and impact heating allows us to simulate the thermal and chemical differentiation of planetesimals during rapid growth, including onion-shell metamorphic structures driven by short-lived 26Al decay. ## Changes - Add `src/accretion.jl` with orbital kinematics, gas and pebble disk structure, Bondi and Hill pebble capture rates, Safronov collision swarms, analytical growth modes, exact 3D spherical shell expansion mapping, impact heating, and boundary advance. - Add `AccretionConfig` schema to `src/config.jl` with validation for mass, radius, and orbital parameter ranges. - Extend `src/simulation.jl` to advance the planetesimal marker boundary, convert sticky-air markers to solid crust, assign initial porosity and bulk iron fractions, and track marker accretion timestamps. - Synchronize marker replenishment in `src/particles.jl` to preserve accretion time arrays during marker injection. - Add unit tests in `test/test_accretion.jl` and `test/test_config.jl`. - Add documentation pages in `docs

prs.title: Add metal-silicate volatile partitioning and core transport
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## What this does This PR adds metal-silicate volatile partitioning parameterizations for H, C, N, and S coupled with conservative advective transport during metallic core segregation. It models local phase equilibration between molten metal and silicate melt, and links liquid metal reference density dynamically to dissolved sulfur content. ## Why Light element dissolution in molten Fe-Ni alloys controls planetary volatile budgets and primitive atmospheric inventories during early planetesimal differentiation. In particular, dissolved sulfur strongly suppresses carbon solubility in metallic liquids while moderately altering nitrogen partitioning. This chemical mechanism explains why sulfur-rich parent bodies like the group IIAB iron meteorite precursors retain carbon in their silicate mantles and exhibit sub-chondritic C/N ratios. ## Changes - In src/physics.jl, implement partition parameterizations across temperature, pressure, redox state (delta IW), and alloy sulfur content for H (Clesi et al. 2018), C and N (Grewal et al. 2019b, Fischer et al. 2020), and S (Boujibar et al. 2014), alongside domain validation and physical saturation limits. - In src/particles.jl and src/numerics.jl, track marker volatile arrays and advect volatiles with metallic iron flux in apply_metal_segregation! while maintaining mass conservation. - In src/particles.jl, couple liquid metal reference density dynamically to alloy sulfur content to update Stokes settling and Darcy percolation rates. - In

prs.title: Add iron core formation drift-flux solver and coupled benchmarks
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## What this does Transports molten iron metal through porous rock and magma oceans to form planetary cores. Subcycles an explicit finite-volume solver with local Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy limits and flux limiters. Updates markers using pore capacity weights to keep metal within maximum packing limits. Adds gravitational sink heat directly to the thermal solver. Couples local effective viscosity to Stokes droplet settling. ## Why Earlier work set up marker metal data and bulk rock-metal mixtures. This change moves liquid metal through rock pores and melt suspensions, tracking core growth and energy release as planets differentiate. ## Changes - Add `apply_metal_segregation!` in `src/numerics.jl` to solve finite-volume metal drift - Add flux limiters across cell faces to stop overshoots and preserve mass - Update markers using capacity weights to obey the `phi_pack` limit - Add gravitational heat to `assemble_thermal_lse!` and `simulation_loop` in `src/simulation.jl` - Couple effective viscosity matrix `ETA` to Stokes settling - Export `simulation_loop` in `src/Erebus.jl` - Support `:fixed`, `:weber_mean`, and `:weber_turbulent` droplet breakup modes - Add planetesimal core formation benchmarks and movie rendering in `benchmarks/` - Document theoretical formulations in `docs/src/explanations/core_formation.md` - Document benchmark suite and validation in `docs/src/validation/core_formation.md` ## Testing - Ran 15,143 tests in `test/test_core_formation.jl` (all passed) - Checked

releases.author: timlichtenberg
releases.body: This release makes an out-of-table entropy value visible and fixes the mantle melt/solid mass split. - Flag entropy outside the tabulated P-S range in every EOS lookup instead of clamping it silently to a table edge, so a node can no longer freeze at an edge value and a non-finite entropy no longer reads back as a plausible finite property (closes #34 and #28). numpy warns and raises under `strict_range` (the warning is bounded per context so a run that repeatedly leaves the table does not flood the log); JAX propagates a non-finite entropy as NaN and stays `jit`/`grad`/`vmap` compatible. - Split the mantle mass into `M_mantle_liquid = Phi_global * M_mantle` and `M_mantle_solid = (1 - Phi_global) * M_mantle`, so both stay in `[0, M_mantle]` and sum to the same `M_mantle` the helpfile reports, instead of a separate PALEOS-density sum that could exceed the whole (closes #33).

releases.author: timlichtenberg
releases.body: This release adds solver diagnostics and a step-count budget for the CVODE path, and reports the conserved CMB heat flux. - Add a CVODE step budget and a core-temperature excursion diagnostic, so a solve that runs out of steps or drives the core temperature past a set limit is surfaced instead of continuing silently (closes #27). - Report the step-average CMB heat flux in the `F_cmb` column, conserved over the step. - Expose `cvode_output_points` and fix the CVODE step-count logging. - Correct the source citations for the gravitational-separation velocity and the critical Reynolds number, and add tests for the gravitational-separation relative velocity.

releases.author: timlichtenberg
releases.body: ## Highlights Settling-drag viscosity as a config option, and the mass-coordinate mesh refresh (#38): - `separation_viscosity` selects the drag viscosity in the gravitational separation velocity: `"melt"` (default, the single-phase melt viscosity of Abe 1995 and SPIDER) or `"mixture"` (the rheological-transition-blended bulk viscosity). Both engines, single-sourced and validated at config time, active mode logged at solver initialisation. - With `mass_coordinates = true`, basic-node pressure and the flux-path density are refreshed from the solved radii after the mesh solve, as SPIDER does. - Validated in coupled caps-off PROTEUS runs at 80 and 160 levels: with `"mixture"` the CMB temperature collapse is gone and the result is resolution-independent; with `"melt"` the collapse remains. PROTEUS sets `"mixture"` as its coupled default. - Docs describe both modes, the equation with the absolute density contrast, the regime boundaries and their sources. Also in this release: the step-cap log line names the margin that fired (#35), the nightly CI timeout is 120 minutes (#37), the melt-solid mobility docs page, and the shared PROTEUS documentation theme.

releases.author: timlichtenberg
releases.body: ## Highlights - `fwl-io prune` removes dataset versions that no installed manifest references any more (#49). It prints a plan by default and removes only with `--delete`. It keeps anything it cannot prove is a superseded fwl-io download, and skips a version whose lock another process holds. This needs `filelock>=3.29.5`, now the minimum. - A manifest entry can set `files = [...]` to use only part of a Zenodo record (#47). `sync`, `fetch`, `check`, `relocate` and the Dataverse mirror then handle only those files. The shared manifest now declares the 30 datasets that PROTEUS and its modules still fetch from hard-coded records. - `fwl-io fetch` shows a download progress bar (#48). It shows by default when stderr is a terminal, and `--progress` / `--no-progress` override that. The bar needs tqdm, which the new `progress` extra installs (`pip install fwl-io[progress]`); without it the fetch continues with no bar. - Conflicting dataset declarations between installed manifests are reported instead of resolved silently (#46): every provider that takes part in the conflict is dropped, with one message each. - `fwl-io mirror-publish` publishes an existing Dataverse draft dataset (#41). It never creates a dataset. - `fwl-io list` prints a dataset's declared name below its key when the two differ, filtered to printable characters (#42, #44). - A new Explanations page documents the data-governance model: what counts as a data change and how it is reviewed and tested (#43).

releases.author: timlichtenberg
releases.body: MORS fetches the Spada et al. (2013) evolution tracks through fwl-io, like the Baraffe tracks (#62). The grid is pinned in the MORS manifest as one archive with a fixed Zenodo record and checksum, and unpacks into `star/tracks/spada_2013/r15729101/fs255_grid` below `FWL_DATA`. The unpacked tracks are identical to the previous `stellar_evolution_tracks/Spada/fs255_grid` tree, and `StarEvo` returns the same values from both. A tree under the old location is not moved, so the grid downloads once more after upgrading. The compiled Spada grid is now cached in the user cache directory, keyed on the track directory and a fingerprint of its files, so a changed tree never serves a grid compiled from old data. Parallel jobs on a cold cache no longer corrupt it, a corrupt cache file is recompiled instead of stopping `StarEvo`, and `Value()` reuses the loaded default grid. The Zenodo and OSF download code is removed, and with it the `osfclient` and `zenodo_get` dependencies. This release still requires `fwl-io>=26.7.22`. Other changes: - The documentation uses the shared PROTEUS theme, with the fonts served from the repository. - The nightly caches the track data under a key derived from the pinned datasets, so it follows a re-pinned dataset instead of refetching every night. - The code style check passes on the new theme assets, and a test fails when a pre-commit exclusion stops matching a file (#57, #58). - The nightly check of the Baraffe registry against Zenodo retries three times an

releases.author: timlichtenberg
releases.body: Parsed PALEOS tables are now cached per process and each file is read once, with a faster structured reader; a 2-phase adiabat call drops from 15-21 s to 6-8 s on the first call and under 1 s after, and a super-liquidus structure solve in PROTEUS from minutes to seconds (#93). A table path that is not a regular file raises FileNotFoundError again, as PROTEUS expects for a missing table (#104). The JAX structure path covers more cases: NaN nodes of the density grids are filled so hot surfaces stay on JAX (#103), the node temperature comes from temperature_arrays (#102), the right-hand side is continuous at zero pressure (#99), and each JAX cache entry is tied to the functions it was built from (#101). The batch PALEOS mushy zone takes its liquidus from the table (#100). A structure solve now fails loudly instead of returning a bad profile: at a non-finite EOS density (#98) and on a failed solve, while a surface stop is padded with the stop state (#94). The SPIDER EOS tables are filled within each pressure column (#90), the P-S tables carry validity masks and the adiabat ends are pinned (#92), and the nightly 2-phase agreement tests no longer crash their workers (#89).

releases.author: timlichtenberg
releases.body: The mushy_zone_factor (mzf) applies to the unified PALEOS EOS family (PALEOS:iron, PALEOS:MgSiO3, PALEOS:H2O, PALEOS-API:iron/MgSiO3/H2O, Chabrier:H) and to PALEOS-2phase materials, not only the tabulated two-phase path. For the unified path, which has no tabulated solidus, mzf in [0.7, 1.0] sets the solidus as a constant fraction of the liquidus; mzf = 1.0 leaves every configured EOS unchanged. At the collapsed melting boundary T_liq == T_sol, the NumPy and JAX two-phase paths both route equality to the solid table, so the phase label and the density lookup agree there. validate_config rejects mzf < 1.0 when no mzf-capable EOS is configured. Per-EOS mzf overrides are read from the TOML config for each unified component (#86). The PALEOS unified tables are fetched from the v1.3.0 data release, and a data download now verifies that the expected files are present before it is trusted (#84).

releases.name: Esqueleto
releases.author: MarijnJ0
releases.body: # 🍃 Obliqua v1.0.0 — Esqueleto🪐 First tagged release of **Obliqua**, a Julia package for computing multiphase tidal dissipation in planetary interiors: tidal Love numbers and the resulting volumetric/global heating rate across solid, partially molten (mush), and fluid mantle layers. Given a body's forcing frequency spectrum (orbital mean motion, spin rate, eccentricity) and a radial interior profile (density, viscosity, shear/bulk moduli, porosity, permeability), Obliqua returns the complex tidal Love number, the radial heating profile (W/m³), and the integrated global tidal power (W). ## 🌋 Physics coverage - **Solid-phase dissipation** — six interchangeable solvers with different applications: - `solid0d`: uniform-interior Love number only (no radial heating profile) - `solid1d`, `solid1d-relax`: radially resolved heating from the full strain tensor - `solid1d-mush`, `solid1d-mush-relax`: extensions for partially molten (mush) layers - `solid1d-equil-relax`: equilibrium-tide limit, used automatically whenever the forcing frequency is (numerically) zero - **Fluid-phase dissipation** — `fluid0d` (uniform) and `fluid1d` (Rayleigh-drag heating with configurable drag efficiency and scale-height treatment) - **Mush/phase-boundary interpolation** — `interp` smooths the heating profile and Love number across solid–fluid interfaces so multi-layer bodies don't produce discontinuous heating at the boundary - **Rheology models** — Maxwell, Andrade (with configurable exponent α), and pur

It bounds the core-temperature drop on the solid adiabat just below the solidus, where the melt-fraction cap goes blind because a fully solid cell's melt fraction can no longer move. entries.title: Lower default centre of the rheological transition
entries.text: The default centre of the rheological transition in melt fraction is lower. It shifts the viscosity blend and the reported rheological front in the interior modules, so runs that rely on the default give different results.

entries.title: Smaller default interior grain size
entries.text: The default grain size of the interior is now smaller. Runs that do not set it explicitly use the new value and can give a different interior evolution.

entries.title: Aragog step caps are off by default
entries.text: The per-step melt fraction, temperature and entropy caps of the coupled Aragog interior are now off by default. On a benign freezing front they sliced the coupled step into many small steps. An explicit zero value for a cap is now rejected when the config loads.

entries.title: Settling drag viscosity choice, mixture default for coupled runs
entries.text: Aragog now offers a choice of drag viscosity in the gravitational separation velocity, and coupled PROTEUS runs default to the mixture viscosity. The release notes report that this removes a collapse of the core-mantle boundary temperature seen with the melt viscosity. The option is also passed to the JAX solver.

entries.title: Aragog entropy range, mass split and boundary fixes
entries.text: Aragog now flags entropy outside the tabulated range instead of clamping it silently, and splits the mantle mass into melt and solid parts that sum to the reported total. The reported core-mantle boundary heat flux is now the conserved step average. Merged fixes also correct core boundary heating and mesh node placement.

entries.title: Super-liquidus start is solved on the interior tables
entries.text: The super-liquidus initial condition is now solved on the interior entropy tables against their own liquidus, for every structure module. Runs without a Zalmoxis structure start from different temperatures and entropies than before. An unreachable superheat now gives a warning or an error.

entries.title: Mushy zone factor applies to the whole PALEOS family
entries.text: The mushy zone factor now acts on the whole PALEOS equation of state family, not only the tabulated two-phase path. A value that gives a non-sharp phase boundary changes the solidus and the density in runs that set it.

entries.title: Zalmoxis structure solves fail instead of returning bad profiles
entries.text: A Zalmoxis structure solve now stops at a non-finite equation of state density and raises an error on a failed solve, instead of returning a faulty profile. The solver paths for JAX and for hot surfaces also changed.

entries.title: New AGNI integration defaults and surface roughness
entries.text: The hydrostatic integration defaults passed to AGNI changed, with a new Hill radius limit, and the default surface roughness length is larger. AGNI also handles atmospheres that become gravitationally unbound more carefully, and it updated its solar abundance data.

entries.title: Satellite options removed from the orbit config
entries.text: The old satellite and orbit evolution options of the orbit config were removed. Planet-satellite orbit models now come with the Obliqua module, and configs that used the removed options must be updated.

entries.title: Erebus.jl plastic iteration limits and reproducible seeds
entries.text: Erebus.jl now rolls back and halves the timestep when plastic iterations fail to converge, and the old iteration count options were removed in favour of new limits. Runs with a fixed seed now give the same result for any thread count, so the reference results changed.

entries.title: AGNI aerosols and optical depth photosphere
entries.text: AGNI can now include aerosols from pre-computed scattering data or from Mie theory, and PROTEUS exposes them. The photosphere can be set from optical depth at a chosen wavelength instead of a fixed pressure. The refractory vapour list matches the species AGNI has thermodynamic data for.

entries.title: Obliqua tides and orbit models in PROTEUS
entries.text: The Obliqua module computes multiphase tidal Love numbers and heating in the planet, and PROTEUS now couples it. Three orbit models cover star-planet and planet-satellite evolution, including evection resonance. Pre-generated lookup tables can replace repeated tide calculations, and the solid models now agree closely on dissipation where they are stable.

entries.title: Erebus.jl planetesimal accretion, core formation and volatiles
entries.text: Erebus.jl now models planetesimal growth by pebble and planetesimal accretion, iron core formation with volatile partitioning, redox buffering, and a coupled atmosphere with envelope capture and hydrodynamic escape.

entries.title: Erebus.jl matrix-free solvers, GPU and MPI
entries.text: Erebus.jl can now solve the Stokes-Darcy system matrix-free with Krylov methods and a multigrid preconditioner. It runs on GPUs and splits the domain over processes with MPI.

entries.title: Faster PALEOS structure solves in Zalmoxis
entries.text: Zalmoxis now caches parsed PALEOS tables once per process and reads each file once. According to the release notes, repeated adiabat and structure calls become much faster.

entries.title: Pixi as an alternative environment manager
entries.text: PROTEUS can now be set up with pixi as an alternative to the existing environment manager.

entries.title: Newer Julia default across the ecosystem
entries.text: PROTEUS now defaults to a newer Julia release and deprecates an older one. Obliqua updates its Julia support to match, and Erebus.jl now requires a newer Julia.

entries.title: Builds with GCC 16
entries.text: SOCRATES now exports its wrapper symbols as public, so builds with GCC 16 load correctly. PROTEUS raised the SOCRATES and AGNI pins for this and pins gcc on macOS CI.

entries.title: Newer Aragog, Zalmoxis and fwl-io required
entries.text: PROTEUS now requires newer releases of Aragog, Zalmoxis and fwl-io. Update these packages in your environment before the next run.

entries.title: Aragog CVODE run stops at setup without CVODE
entries.text: A run with the Aragog CVODE solver now stops at setup when the CVODE package cannot be imported, instead of failing later.

entries.title: More robust get commands
entries.text: The proteus get command now writes a per-user logfile in the temporary directory, and the get install scripts resolve a target path that does not exist yet.

entries.title: fwl-io prune, file filters and progress bar
entries.text: fwl-io can now remove dataset versions that no installed manifest references, and it shows a plan before any deletion. Manifests can select a subset of the files of a record, fetches show a progress bar, and a mirrored dataset takes the licence of its source record.

entries.title: Spada tracks fetched through fwl-io
entries.text: MORS fetches the Spada evolution tracks through fwl-io with a pinned checksum. The grid downloads again to a new location after an upgrade. MORS no longer depends on two download clients.

entries.title: PALEOS tables from the v1.3.0 data release
entries.text: PROTEUS and Zalmoxis now fetch the PALEOS unified equation of state tables from the v1.3.0 data release. A download is checked for completeness before it is trusted.

entries.title: Aragog relicensed under Apache-2.0
entries.text: Aragog is now released under the Apache-2.0 licence, and PROTEUS requires the Apache-licensed release.

entries.title: Helpfile columns added and removed
entries.text: Several helpfile columns changed: one for the core-mantle boundary node temperature was added, the AGNI and Obliqua outputs add columns for new species, orbit and position quantities, and one initial core-mantle boundary column was removed. Zero-filled SPIDER and atmodeller columns are now filled.

entries.title: Resume and miscibility guards
entries.text: Resumed Aragog runs now restore the stored core-mantle boundary entropy gradient and mesh surface pressure. A resume no longer anchors the magma temperature to the surface temperature and picks the right snapshot when filenames collide. Global miscibility is now rejected for every structure module.

entries.title: Agent instructions in ZEPHYRUS moved to AGENTS.md
entries.text: ZEPHYRUS moved its agent instructions to the AGENTS.md format, the same format proposed for PROTEUS.

entries.title: Accretion module with Morrigan
entries.text: A new accretion module grows the planet by giant impacts during magma ocean evolution. Morrigan follows a system of embryos, a timeline option replays an impact history from a file, and a dummy option builds one from scaling laws.

entries.title: Volatile trapping behind the freezing front
entries.text: A new option traps dissolved volatiles in the solid mantle during crystallisation, based on pore melt drainage across the freezing front. It is off by default. A correction to the atmosphere budget of a frozen mantle applies even with trapping off.

entries.title: Reference data through fwl-io
entries.text: PROTEUS would fetch and read all reference data through fwl-io manifests with pinned checksums. A run would require exactly the tables its equation of state reads and would stop before it starts when data is missing.

entries.title: Inference config validation and failure handling
entries.text: Inference runs would validate the reference config like PROTEUS does and reject bad configs before any computation. Failed runs are recorded in a table, and runs with the same stellar spectrum can share one prepared spectral file.

entries.title: ZEPHYRUS escape regime dispatcher
entries.text: A new dispatcher assigns each planetary state one of six escape regimes, returns one bulk mass-loss rate, and splits it over species. It is a standalone interface for now, and the PROTEUS coupling follows in a separate pull request.

entries.title: Shared agent instructions in AGENTS.md
entries.text: PROTEUS would move its agent instructions to AGENTS.md, with a shared block for all modules and a daily check that module repositories stay in sync.

entries.title: Aragog radionuclide heating and exit status
entries.text: Two Aragog pull requests would remove NaN heating from zero-amplitude radionuclides and make the aragog run command exit with a non-zero status when the integration fails.
